simple.meaning: תְּשׁוּקָה (tᵉshûwqâh) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a longing.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 3:16. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּשׁוּקָה (H8669) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: תְּשׁוּקָה (tᵉshûwqâh) / H8669 is traced through Genesis 3:16, Genesis 4:7, Song of Songs 7:11 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H8669. teshuqah [ תְּשׁוּקָה ] noun feminine longing ; — of woman for man, תְּשׁוּקָתֵח אֶלאִֿישֵׁח Gen 3:16 (J); of man for woman, תְּשׁוּקָתוֺ וְאֵלַי לְדוֺדִי אֲנִי Cant 7:11; of beast to devour, figurative תְּשׁוּקָתוֺ אֵלֶיךָ 4:7 (J). ( ᵐ5 ἀποστροφή Genesis, ἐπιστροφή Canticles, whence Nes Marg. 6 proposes תְּשׁוּבָתֵךְ 3:16 , which Ball Hpt reads in all; but how explain the unusual and striking word in MT?).
